glossary.Acute: Coming on suddenly and lasting a short time.
glossary.Type A: The influenza type that infects humans and animals and can undergo antigenic shift.
glossary.Type B: The influenza type found mainly in humans; causes seasonal outbreaks but not pandemics.
glossary.Respiratory droplets: Small drops from coughs and sneezes that carry virus a short distance.
glossary.Close contact: Being near an infected person, close enough to breathe their droplets or touch shared surfaces.
glossary.Immunosuppression: A weakened immune system, from disease or drugs such as steroids or chemotherapy.
glossary.Tachycardia: A heart rate over 100 beats per minute.
glossary.Antigens: Molecules on a germ's surface that the immune system recognises.
glossary.Seasonal outbreaks: Yearly winter waves of flu caused by drifted strains.
glossary.Pleuritic chest pain: Sharp chest pain worse on breathing in, from inflamed pleura.
glossary.Productive cough: A cough that brings up sputum.
glossary.Coarse crackles: Loud, low-pitched crackles heard with a stethoscope, from secretions in the airways.
glossary.Infiltrates: Hazy or dense shadows on an X-ray where the lung is filled with fluid, pus or cells.
glossary.Pulmonary embolism: A blood clot blocking an artery in the lungs.
glossary.Hypoxia: Low oxygen levels in the blood or tissues.
glossary.Clinical diagnosis: A diagnosis made from symptoms and signs alone, without a confirming test.
glossary.Community circulation: How widely a virus is spreading among the public at the time.
glossary.Supportive care: Treatment that relieves symptoms while the body clears the infection.
glossary.Ibuprofen: An anti-inflammatory painkiller (NSAID) that also lowers fever.
glossary.Heart failure: The heart cannot pump enough blood to meet the body's needs.
glossary.Antiviral: A drug that stops a virus from multiplying.
glossary.Low sats: Low oxygen saturation on pulse oximetry.
glossary.IV: Intravenous: given directly into a vein.
glossary.ICU: Intensive care unit, for patients needing organ support such as ventilation.
glossary.Mechanical ventilation: A machine breathing for the patient through a tube in the airway.
glossary.Vaccination: Giving a vaccine to train the immune system to recognise an infection.
glossary.Comorbidities: Other long-term illnesses a patient has alongside the main one.
glossary.TIV-HD: High-dose trivalent influenza vaccine, used in people aged 65 and over.
glossary.QIV-HD: High-dose quadrivalent influenza vaccine, covering four flu strains.
glossary.TIVr: Recombinant trivalent influenza vaccine, made without growing virus in eggs.
glossary.QIVr: Recombinant quadrivalent influenza vaccine, covering four strains.
glossary.Point mutations: Changes in single letters of a gene's code.
glossary.Immune evasion: A germ's ability to escape recognition by existing antibodies.
glossary.Subtype: A strain defined by its haemagglutinin and neuraminidase types, such as H1N1.
glossary.Co-infection: Infection with two strains or germs at the same time.
glossary.Respiratory epithelium: The cell lining of the airways, with cilia and mucus to trap and clear germs.
glossary.Epidemics: Sudden rises in cases of a disease within a population.
